title: A Cipher for the Will
premise: When the coffin of Ashford Bell, founder of the river town of Marrow's Bend, is found empty during a cemetery relocation, retired detective Silas Quintana is pulled back into a town that has always kept him at arm's length. The empty grave reopens the one case Silas was forced to abandon thirty years ago: the disappearance of his partner, Ada Voss, whose death was ruled an accident on the same night Bell supposedly died. As Silas digs through forged records and the town's carefully curated memory, they discover Bell faked his death to escape blackmail—and that Ada uncovered it first. At the anniversary dinner where Marrow's Bend celebrates its founding, Silas confronts the last living conspirator, exposes the truth, and finally claims a place in the town that once erased them.
about_author: Petra Winterbourne is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records before turning to fiction, a background that infuses her mysteries with the texture of paper trails and buried ledgers. She writes from a converted ferry house on the northern coast, where she collects obituaries and insists every town she invents deserves its own history no one wants read aloud.

chapters.title: The Weight of Absence
chapters.summary: Silas Quintana closes up their failing bookshop and reflects, in close third person, on three 'accidents' they quietly solved and the solitude that invisibility buys. A letter arrives announcing the exhumation of town founder Ashford Bell for the centennial relocation. The emotional beat is wary contentment about to crack—Silas recognizes the letterhead as the same firm that closed Ada Voss's case decades ago.

chapters.title: What the Ground Kept
chapters.summary: At the cemetery, Silas watches the vault opened: the coffin holds only river stones and a rotted ledger page bearing Ada's handwriting. POV shifts briefly to young gravedigger Tomas Reyes, who found the anomaly and fears he'll be blamed. The beat is dread sharpening into purpose—the past has literally surfaced, and Silas cannot look away this time.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: Silas visits the police archive and finds Ada's file suspiciously thin, pages replaced with carbon copies. Police Chief Ibarra warns them off, but her trembling hands suggest fear, not contempt. Flashbacks braid with the present as Silas recalls being ordered to stop investigating Ada's drowning. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve; the town's official memory is a locked room and Silas still has a key.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Liars
chapters.summary: In the historical society's basement, Silas cross-references Bell's financial records and finds payments continuing after his supposed death—signed by his widow, Cordelia. A confrontation with elderly Cordelia yields a half-confession wrapped in deflection. POV stays with Silas. The beat is the thrill of the hunt returning, shadowed by guilt that pursuing truth may cost Silas the fragile belonging they've built.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Silas infiltrates the centennial dinner preparations, posing as a volunteer, and discovers someone has been sanitizing the archives—fresh glue, removed pages. They catch archivist Maren Hale burning documents behind the society hall. Maren, terrified, reveals she was paid by an anonymous trust. Beat: paranoia rises; the conspiracy isn't history, it's ongoing, and Silas is now visible to it.

chapters.title: River Stones
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes, frightened after being followed, comes to the bookshop at night. He shows Silas where the stones in the coffin came from—a private stretch of riverbank owned by the Hollis family, whose patriarch was Bell's business partner. Silas realizes the stones were a message or a marker. Beat: alliance forms across generations; Silas feels, for the first time, less alone in the case than Ada ever was.

chapters.title: A Case Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Silas reconstructs Ada's final week using her hidden notes, sewn into a book that has sat unsold on Silas's own shelves for thirty years. The notes prove Ada knew Bell was alive and was meeting him the night she drowned. Devastated, Silas understands they were given the book by someone who wanted them to find it eventually. Beat: heartbreak transmuted into clarity—the case was never cold, only waiting.

chapters.title: The Trust
chapters.summary: Following the money, Silas identifies the anonymous trust funding the cover-up: administered by Judge Ellery Hollis, son of Bell's partner, now the town's most respected citizen. A tense parlor interview where Ellery offers Silas a place on the anniversary dais—an offer of belonging in exchange for silence. Beat: temptation rendered concrete; everything Silas ever wanted, priced at Ada's erasure.

chapters.title: Before the Toast
chapters.summary: On the eve of the dinner, Chief Ibarra privately gives Silas the original case file she's protected for years, admitting her father helped bury the truth. Silas lays out evidence for the whole conspiracy: Bell alive until 1998, drowned by Hollis when the blackmail turned mutual, Ada killed for witnessing it. Beat: quiet fury and solidarity; the machinery of silence begins to turn against itself.

chapters.title: Raise the Glass
chapters.summary: At the anniversary dinner, Silas stands during the founding toast and reads Ada's final note aloud, producing the ledger, the file, and Ellery's recorded confession from the parlor wire Ibarra wore. Ellery is arrested as the room's memory shatters and reforms. In the aftermath, townspeople begin bringing Silas their own unanswered questions. Final beat: belonging earned not by invisibility but by truth—Silas locks the shop, leaves the light on, and finally says Ada's name out loud.
